verdicts.strongest_argument: The claim is built on a stale document that the snapshot made look current, and every leg of it predates a print the market already answered. The brief carries `source_date: 2026-09-02` for the Pure Storage peer quote, but that is the FETCH timestamp, not the publication date: the stored body itself contains the article's own schema block, `"datePublished":"2026-02-26T05:02:26Z"`, and the headline is 'Pure Storage Inc (PSTG) Q4 2026 Earnings Call Highlights' - PSTG's fiscal Q4 call, held in late February 2026. So the peer's list-price increase and its product-gross-margin caveat have been public for six months, and the 'number and a quarter' the hunter says the peer put on it was PSTG's own Q1 FY27, guided in February. The second leg is dated in its own URL slug: storageswiss.com/2026/05/06 - four months old. The third leg is NetApp's own commentary on its own earnings call, reported 2026-05-29. All three therefore predate NetApp's 2026-05-28 print, which the market answered with a +22.39% reaction on expanding margins - by far the largest move in the seven-event history against a 3.43% median - and the hunter concedes exactly this in its own band note: 'NetApp resolved this same cost worry favourably once already in May.' A cost narrative that was fully public before a print the stock rose 22% on is not an unexploited edge into the next print; it is a resolved question the market re-underwrote at a higher price. The DRAM/NAND squeeze is also structural and mainstream rather than obscure - the HPE capture in this same run carries an item headlined 'CEO Says Networking Segment More Insulated From Memory Supply Squeeze', which is how widely the memory-cost frame was circulating in the same days. Finally the finding's tape argument is contradicted by its own baseline: it says 'NetApp would not be sitting near an all-time high on demand-led upgrades' if this were priced, but the sealed baseline puts spot at 180.77, which is 12.71% BELOW the 52-week high with run_up_5d of -6.75% and run_up_20d of -3.12%. The stock had already given back the demand-led melt-up before the print. I leave 12 points because no captured document explicitly quantifies elevated NAND against NetApp's product gross margin line, so the specific P&L arithmetic is reachable rather than drawn out.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Pure Storage's Q4 FY26 call, from late February 2026, is where the list-price increase 'due to a dramatic rise in component costs' and the product-gross-margin caveat were disclosed - six months before this print, and three months before NetApp's own May print.
The structural-reallocation thesis and the 20-22% demand vs 15-17% supply figures were published on 2026-05-06, per the article's own URL slug - before NetApp's May 28 print.
NetApp itself acknowledged cost rises from 'higher NAND pricing' on its May call while guiding a strong outlook - company commentary given to the whole market.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The cost worry was priced in a measured event and resolved upward: the 2026-05-28 amc print, which post-dates all three of the finding's sources, moved +22.39% against a 3.43% seven-event median. Into this print the tape is the opposite of the finding's description - spot 180.77, -12.71% from the 52-week high, run_up_5d -6.75%, run_up_20d -3.12% - so the 'sitting near an all-time high' premise the non-pricing argument depends on is false against the sealed baseline. Baseline quality is sound (fits_cadence, 7 events), so no defective anchor is doing work here.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A peer or supplier datapoint dated after 2026-05-28 - i.e. after NetApp's last print - that put a fresh number on flash input costs for the July quarter, rather than a February call and a May sector piece the May print already digested.

interactions: none across findings (one claim), but internally the three cited sources are not independent in time: all three predate NetApp's 2026-05-28 print, so the 'source cluster' is one vintage of information, not corroboration across the run-in.
